answer_1.quote: To address this question, we designed an openended generation experiment that uses the same scenarios ... allows us to examine whether LLMs employ a similarly diverse and context-sensitive set of politeness strategies as humans ...

answer_2.quote: We report Spearman correlation and mean squared error (MSE) between LLM and human responses as an overall measure of fit (see Table).

answer_3.quote: We used LLMs (GPT-4.1 and Claude-3.7-Sonnet) as annotators, following best practices .
criteria: politeness strategy labeling (positive politeness, negative politeness, off-record, bald-on-record)

answer_4.quote: We conducted a two-alternative forced-choice evaluation, with 156 human evaluators ... Evaluators made five judgments per scenario: (1) comparing human vs. LLM responses, (2-3) comparing goal-congruent vs. goal-incongruent responses for both sources, and (4-5) comparing rating-congruent vs. rating-incongruent responses for both sources.
answer_4.guideline: Pairwise forced-choice comparisons assessing preference for human vs. LLM, goal congruence, and rating congruence.
